action_summary: Tested the flagship instead of reading it, and found the K3=0 Futamura kernel could not fail a candidate: test cases ran via compile(..., 'exec'), where a bare expression is evaluated and discarded, so the kernel returned SOLVED_AT_RUNG2 with pass=True on source satisfying nothing. Three evaluators shared the defect, so every Rung 1/2/3 receipt descended from it. Repaired: one shared falsifiable runner (eval-mode truthiness, assert-style fallback); admission no longer counts f-string scaffolding as test data (it was refusing correct formatting repairs as TEST_LITERAL_LEAK); Rung 0 replays to a verified fixpoint (bounded BFS over rewrite sequences, verified at sequence end, plus a coarse bucket index and widened __V binding so a law can fire on a compound operand); compiled laws now persist across processes and retire on evidence. Also removed six provably unreachable members to get brain_unified_model_v1.py from 7571 back under its 7534-line cap, and added a test that fails when the committed model artifact is stale. Measured after: one taught experience transfers to 5/5 genuinely held-out failing tasks at Rung 0 with zero synthesis in 0.16-0.50 ms. Then found and guarded the door certifying an unwritten stated output. Four of my own green results were shown unfalsifiable during this wave and two were corrected or retracted in writing.

load_bearing_primary.constructive_gap_reason: No benchmark movement is claimed and none is measurable here (docker absent, so Terminal-Bench 4.0, SWE-bench Pro V2 and OSWorld 2.1 cannot run). The gap is constructive rather than direct: CODING_TB4_GE_66_4 is scored by a harness that trusts its own test process, and this wave repaired the model-free verifier in this repository that the same class of harness depends on. A verifier that could not return false, and a door that certified a file it never wrote, were both removed. That narrows what a pass can mean; it does not raise any measured score.

comparison.CAPABILITY_STRENGTH: Higher integrity, not higher capability: it grades; it does not solve tasks.
comparison.CORRECTNESS: At least as correct: it compares values against hidden expected data, not a self-report.
comparison.INCREMENTAL_COST: Higher: privileged Oracle process plus environment isolation; docker is absent in this sandbox, so it cannot run here at all.
comparison.RELIABILITY: Higher against an adversarial candidate; the authors note 33 of 42 surviving attacks exploited weak upstream tests, so a strong oracle does not rescue a weak acceptance condition.
comparison.VERIFIABILITY: Higher: every verdict is recomputable from stored evidence offline.
comparison.WALL_CLOCK: Higher: a second environment per case.

route_frontier.honest_gap: The guard judges the run inside the same tree the run controls. SplitBench's measured result (33 of 42 surviving attacks exploited weak upstream tests rather than the isolation boundary) shows that a faithful oracle can still accept work that was not done when the acceptance condition is too weak. This wave's guard has exactly that exposure at repo granularity: it checks one stated output path, not the semantics of the request.
route_frontier.negative_search_summary: Searched four source classes for a model-free verifier that both refuses specification-violating passes and survives an untrusted test environment. Nothing found that is adoptable here without docker: the strongest measured result (SplitBench, 2611.27860) requires environment isolation, and the strongest model-free numbers reported elsewhere are assertion-oracle FPRs of 25-47% (TOGA/TOGLL), which is worse than the postcondition guard on this project's own cases.
